Q1493320.label: 1935 Canadian federal election
Q1493320.summary: The 1935 Canadian federal election was held on October 14, 1935, to elect members of the House of Commons of Canada of the 18th Parliament of Canada. The Liberal Party of William Lyon Mackenzie King won a majority government, defeating Prime Minister R. B. Bennett's Conservatives.

Q637768.label: José María Lemus
Q637768.img: Arzobispo monseñor Luis Chavez y González y el presidente Teniente Coronel José María Lémus durante un acto Oficial, 1958.jpg
Q637768.summary: José María Lemus López was president of El Salvador from 14 September 1956 to 26 October 1960. Before becoming a president, he served as an undersecretary of defense and a minister of the interior.

Q2344776.label: Democratic Republican Alliance
Q2344776.summary: The Democratic Alliance, originally called Democratic Republican Alliance, was a French political party created in 1901 by followers of Léon Gambetta such as Raymond Poincaré, who would be president of the Council in the 1920s. The party was originally formed as a centre-left gathering of moderate liberals, independent Radicals who rejected the new left-leaning Radical-Socialist Party, and Moderate Republicans, situated at the political centre and to the right of the newly formed Radical-Socialist Party.

Q1164616.label: 2012 French legislative election
Q1164616.summary: Legislative elections were held in France on 10 and 17 June 2012 to select the members of the 14th National Assembly of the Fifth Republic, a little over a month after the presidential election run-off held on 6 May.

Q4709192.label: Albanian constitutional referendum, 1998
Q4709192.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Albania on 22 November 1998. Voters were asked whether they approved of the constitution. It was approved by 93.5% of voters with a turnout of 50.6%, and came into force on 28 November.

Q335688.label: Milorad Dodik
Q335688.summary: Milorad Dodik is a Bosnian Serb politician who served as president of Republika Srpska from 2022 until his removal from office in 2025. Having previously held the office from 2010 to 2018, he also served as the Serb member of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina from 2018 to 2022.

Q84028744.summary: Presidential elections were held in Lithuania on 12 May 2024, alongside a referendum on allowing multiple citizenships. Incumbent President Gitanas Nausėda won re-election to a second term.

Q2379080.label: Northwest Territories division plebiscite, 1982
Q2379080.desc: 1982 referendum creating the Canadian territory of Nunavut
Q2379080.summary: The Northwest Territories division plebiscite was a stand-alone, territory-wide plebiscite conducted on April 14, 1982. This was the first territory-wide plebiscite conducted in Northwest Territories history.

Q1284424.label: 1992 Montenegrin independence referendum
Q1284424.summary: The 1992 Montenegrin sovereignty referendum was the first referendum regarding Montenegrin sovereignty, held on 1 March 1992 in SR Montenegro, a constituent republic of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

Q4393800.label: Åland European Union membership referendum, 1994
Q4393800.summary: A referendum on European Union membership was held in Åland, Finland on 20 November 1994. Although a nationwide referendum had been held in Finland on 16 October, the islands held another separate vote as they were a separate customs jurisdiction. EU membership was approved by 74% of voters.

mentions.c: Finland: 1994 Ålandic European Union membership referendum

Q15293256.label: 2013 Little India riot
Q15293256.summary: The Little India riot took place in the Singaporean subzone of Little India on 8 December 2013 at SST 21:21, after a fatal traffic accident at the road junction of Race Course Road and Tekka Lane caused the death of 33-year-old Indian construction worker Sakthivel Kumaravelu.

Q56121160.label: September 2018 inter-Korean summit
Q56121160.summary: The September 2018 inter-Korean summit was a meeting between South Korean president Moon Jae-in and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un held between 18 and 20 September 2018, in Pyongyang. It was the third and final inter-Korean summit in the 2018–19 Korean peace process.

Q76824392.label: 2019 London Bridge stabbing
Q76824392.img: City of London UK location map.svg
Q76824392.summary: On 29 November 2019, five people were stabbed, two of them fatally, in Central London. The attacker, Usman Khan, was fatally shot by City of London Police.

mentions.c: United Kingdom: Terrorist attack: 2019 London Bridge stabbings

Q137036104.summary: On 26 November 2025, the president of Guinea-Bissau, Umaro Sissoco Embaló, was arrested as part of a coup d'état carried out by Head of the Military Office of the Presidency Brigadier General Dinis Incanha.

Participants: High Military Command for the Restoration of National Security and Public Order

Q121160.label: Guy Parmelin
Q121160.summary: Guy Bernard Parmelin is a Swiss politician and viticulturist who has been a member of the Federal Council since 2016. A member of the Swiss People's Party (SVP/UDC), he is currently the president of Switzerland for 2026, having previously served as president in 2021 and as vice president in 2020 and 2025. Parmelin has also led the Department of Economic Affairs, Education and Research since 2019. He previously led the Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sports between 2016 and 2018.

Q7443272.label: Second Encirclement Campaign against Jiangxi Soviet
Q7443272.desc: 1931 military campaign during the Chinese Civil War
Q7443272.wiki: Second encirclement campaign against the Jiangxi Soviet
Q7443272.summary: The second encirclement campaign against Jiangxi Soviet was a series of battles launched by the Chinese Nationalist Government in the hope of encircling and destroying the Jiangxi Soviet after the previous campaign had failed. The Red Army repelled the encirclement by launching their second counter-encirclement campaign, also called by the communists as the second counter-encirclement campaign at Central Revolutionary Base, in which the local Chinese Red Army successfully defended the Jiangxi Soviet against the Nationalist attacks from April 1, 1931, to May 31, 1931.

Q4871496.label: Battle of Kuala Lumpur
Q4871496.img: Japanese troops mopping up in Kuala Lumpur.jpg
Q4871496.summary: The Battle of Kuala Lumpur was a battle between Japanese invasion forces and the British forces in Kuala Lumpur, in the then capital of the Federated Malay States, a British protectorate. Starting in late December Japanese began bombing the city;ground forces reached the city by 11 January 1942. The battle was part of Empire of Japan's expansive attack across the Pacific in December 1941, invading and attacking all over the Pacific, from Pearl Harbor, striking islands across the Pacific, Philippines, Malaya, Borneo, Burma, and Thailand.

Q830792.label: Mga Offensive
Q830792.summary: The Mga offensive or Third Battle of Lake Ladoga or fifth Sinyavino offensive was an unsuccessful offensive operation by Soviet troops between 22 July and 25 September 1943 to break the siege of Leningrad.

Q2694984.label: Battle of Remagen
Q2694984.img: CROSS THE RHINE WITH DRY FEET COURTESY OF 9TH ARM'D DIV-LUDENDORFF BRIDGE.jpg
Q2694984.summary: The Battle of Remagen was an 18-day battle during the Allied invasion of Germany in World War II. It lasted from 7 to 25 March 1945 when American forces unexpectedly captured the Ludendorff Bridge over the Rhine intact. They were able to hold it against German opposition and build additional temporary crossings. The presence of a bridgehead across the Rhine advanced the Western Allies' planned crossing of the Rhine into the German interior by three weeks.

Q4873032.label: Battle of the Twin Tunnels
Q4873032.summary: The Battle of the Twin Tunnels took place during the Korean War. In which the UN forces inflicted heavy casualties on the People's Volunteer Army (PVA). The "Twin Tunnels" refer to a series of railroad tunnels along the Central Line in eastern Jije-myeon, Yangpyeong County, Gyeonggi Province, South Korea.

Q42886472.label: Operation Lejeune
Q42886472.summary: Operation Lejeune was an operation conducted by the 2nd Brigade, 1st Cavalry Division in Đức Phổ District, Quảng Ngãi Province, South Vietnam, lasting from 7 to 22 April 1967.

Q131364168.label: Operation Dawn of Freedom
Q131364168.summary: Operation Dawn of Freedom refers to a military offensive launched by the Syrian National Army against the Syrian Arab Armed Forces (SAAF) and the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF), targeting the northern Aleppo Governorate region between al-Bab and Tadef within the Operation Euphrates Shield zone.

Q124485448.label: Siege of Babanusa
Q124485448.summary: The siege of Babanusa was a siege of the Sudanese civil war. The siege started when fighting erupted between the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) on 22 January 2024 near Babanusa. On 1 December 2025, RSF took control of the city after a prolonged siege.

Q127220552.label: June 2024 Al-Mawasi refugee camp attack
Q127220552.desc: 2024 Israeli attack on refugee camp in Gaza
Q127220552.summary: On 21 June 2024, Israeli forces attacked refugee tent camps in al-Mawasi, Gaza Strip just outside an area designated as a humanitarian safe zone. The Gaza Health Ministry reported that 25 people were killed and 50 others were injured in the two rounds of bombing. The bombing was the second Israeli bombardment of the al-Mawasi refugee camp in under a month, with an attack on 28 May killing over 21 people and injuring 64 more.

Q5232968.label: Exercitatio Anatomica de Motu Cordis et Sanguinis in Animalibus
Q5232968.wiki: Exercitatio Anatomica de Motu Cordis et Sanguinis in Animalibus
Q5232968.summary: Exercitatio Anatomica de Motu Cordis et Sanguinis in Animalibus, commonly shortened to De Motu Cordis, is the best-known work of royal physician William Harvey, which was first published in 1628 and established the circulation of blood throughout the body. It is a landmark in the history of physiology, with Harvey combining observations, experiments, measurements, and hypotheses in an extraordinary fashion to arrive at his doctrine.

mentions.c: 1628 · Medicine & Health, Biology · University of Oxford

Q84296.label: Ludwig Boltzmann
Q84296.summary: Ludwig Eduard Boltzmann was an Austrian mathematician and theoretical physicist. His greatest achievements were the development of statistical mechanics and the statistical explanation of the second law of thermodynamics. In 1877, he provided the current definition of entropy, , where Ω is the number of microstates whose energy equals the system's energy, interpreted as a measure of the statistical disorder of a system. Max Planck named the constant kB the Boltzmann constant.

Q4201800.summary: The P. L. Kapitza Institute for Physical Problems of the Russian Academy of Sciences was founded in 1934 as a unique initiative to enable Pyotr L. Kapitza to continue his research in the Soviet Union after his return from England. According to Kapitza, the institution was given the somewhat unconventional name Institute for Physical Problems to emphasize that its focus would not be confined to a single area of knowledge. Instead, it would address "known scientific problems, the scope of which will be determined by the personnel, the scientific staff who will work in it."

Q1285960.label: Edmund Beecher Wilson
Q1285960.img: Edmund Beecher Wilson between about 1885 and 1891.jpg
Q1285960.summary: Edmund Beecher Wilson was an American zoologist and geneticist. He wrote one of the most influential textbooks in modern biology, The Cell in Development and Inheritance. He discovered the chromosomal XY sex-determination system in 1905. Nettie Stevens independently made the same discovery the same year and published shortly thereafter.
